Changes and preservation

serve/server.py adds ConvCacheLog and the official conversation_cache_view aggregation. Service owns one reader and adds conversation_cache to its existing /metrics result. Engine INFO supplies budget/slots; the existing status-lock snapshots supply history and reuse totals. The reader supplies only log-observed parked state. There is no replacement of server, inference code, cache operations, model settings or lifecycle ownership.

The engine startup code now stores self.log_start and a single self.log_cursor tuple (log path, start offset, unique run object) before process launch. Restart refreshes the tuple. Metrics reads that tuple as one assignment, avoiding a mixed path/offset/run snapshot. Older/fake engines can use their existing log_path and log_start attributes. Lazy/no-log engines return unavailable parked details. The old READY failure hint/tail behavior remains.

The reader serializes key, position, file identity, reads, parsing and returned snapshots with a private mutex. Service releases status_lock before entering the reader, so it introduces no lock-order cycle. Each read is limited to 1MiB from an opened file's fstat snapshot. Complete newline-delimited records are consumed once; a partial tail remains for the next poll. Lines longer than 4096 characters are skipped and mark the view incomplete, bounding regex work. Numeric values are limited to uint64 and 20 digits. Malformed values cannot fail the HTTP request. Observed park/restore counters also stop at uint64.

Path/start/run changes reset the reader. File truncation/replacement resets observations and marks history incomplete. When more than 1MiB is unread, the reader retains the tail, discards its first potentially partial line and marks incomplete. Missing/unreadable logs set available=false; absent log configuration clears old observations. Only numeric fields and fixed event labels reach metrics; raw log content/path and credentials are not exposed.

Current native log formats were read without changing src/program/generate.cpp: line6408 emits parked/skipped token counts, parked entries, bytes and evictions; line8535 emits restored token counts, parked entries and bytes; line6371 emits dropped superseded entries and parked count. The regex matches these forms. Because the dropped form omits updated bytes, the view returns bytes=null until the next snapshot-bearing record. It does not reuse an old byte count as a current measurement.

This is a log observer, not an authoritative native-pool query. Unlogged cache clears/nonfinite invalidations cannot be reconstructed. Existing nonfinite, SAVE/RESTORE and cache admission remain untouched. The request-count/reused-request fields cover the retained 500-request history, matching upstream; token totals use existing server totals. Incomplete log history makes park/restore totals counts of retained observed lines, not exact all-run totals.

The web files add one Conversation cache card: slots/RAM budget bars, reuse facts, park/restore/eviction counts and last switch. No-log hides the parked bars and displays an unavailable message. Incomplete history has a note; unknown bytes display Unknown. CSS includes the official scoped card rules and the 1000px single-column layout. Existing Xe model_switcher and Recent requests Reused column remain, with no duplicate column. Windows winjob, replicas, native/GPU/CPU inference, model configuration and defaults are outside the change.

Source fixtures, all unexecuted

serve/test_monitor.py keeps existing tests and adds the official ConversationCacheCard class, adapted to test_chat_template.jinja. Its three upstream tests cover incremental log forms/current offset/partial dropped line, MockEngine plus loopback HTTP metrics/chat, and required card DOM IDs/renderer text.

Five added boundaries cover partial lines counted once; no-log/unreadable files; run identity/current offset and truncation reset; an actual 256-byte bounded read through a real-file-backed mock plus malformed numeric fields; 32 concurrent Service.metrics calls with one park counted once; and a Python fake-engine constructor/restart recording a new log offset/run identity. The fake engine has a patched 5s READY deadline and existing close ownership. No fake process, HTTP service, imported module or test was run by the implementer. Dropped bytes=null is asserted. String-based DOM checks do not prove browser rendering.

Main remaining checks

1. Read all five diffs, cursor/reset/reader locking and bounded-read behavior. Confirm native engine source, model settings, Xe model switcher and existing Reused column are preserved.
2. Run: python3 -m unittest serve.test_monitor serve.test_ready_timeout serve.test_restart_waiters serve.test_server serve.test_parallel -v. Then run the full affected CPU/fake-HTTP regression if warranted. Observe fake child/pipe/socket closure under Main's finite owner.
3. Run fresh changed-file Python/JS/CSS/HTML, codespell, gitleaks and REUSE lints. No formatter or blanket exemptions. Review overly long source lines and any environment-specific typing diagnostics directly.
4. Add/review boundaries for permission failures, same-offset new runs, file replacement, long partial lines, the 4096-character parser cap, maximum numeric fields and concurrent metrics. Existing reader tests cover only the cases described, not every filesystem race.
5. If desired, Main alone verifies browser states: enabled/disabled/no-log/incomplete, unknown bytes, bar widths, narrow layout and escaping. Browser, CSS behavior and live native park/restore correctness remain unverified. No GPU/model measurement or full262144/RESTORE qualification is claimed or needed for the source port.

Main alone commits/pushes after review/tests/lints. Original qualification results are unchanged and no artifacts were deleted.
